proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a law \(P\) satisfying the stated fixed-support and constant-rank conditions.  Put \(m_P=|\mathcal S_P|\), enumerate \(\mathcal S_P\), and identify a function on \(\mathcal S_P\) with its vector of cell values.  Since \(P\) is in the relative interior of this stratum, \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S_P\).  Hence \(W_P\) is positive definite and \(W_P^{-1}\) used in \(\text{def:efficiency-handle}\) exists.

We first verify that the construction in that definition is the observed-law parameterization of the restricted model.  Conditional on \((D=d,Z=j)\), consistency and no anticipation identify the observed variables through date \(2\) with the corresponding potential path.  The type-conditional first-order Markov property therefore gives, for every legal cell \(s=(d,x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(O=s)
 &=P(D=d)\sum_{j=1}^2P(Z=j\mid D=d)
       P(X_0=x_0\mid Z=j,D=d)\\
 &\quad\times P(X_1=x_1\mid X_0=x_0,Z=j,D=d)
       P(X_2=x_2\mid X_1=x_1,Z=j,D=d)\\
 &\quad\times P(X_3=x_3\mid X_2=x_2,Z=j,D=d)
       P(X_4=x_4\mid X_3=x_3,Z=j,D=d).
\end{aligned}                                           \tag{1}
\]
The common date-\(2\) transition assumption makes the third transition factor in \((1)\) equal to \(Q_j[x_1,x_2]\).  In the control cohort, the common first-post untreated transition and common date-\(4\) untreated transition make the last two factors \(U_j[x_2,x_3]\) and \(L_j[x_3,x_4]\).  In the treated cohort, they are the factual treated kernels \(V_j[x_2,x_3]\) and \(T_{4,j}^1[x_3,x_4]\).  Absorption fixes the exit rows and forbids precisely the coordinates outside \(\mathcal G\).  Thus \((1)\) is exactly the polynomial cell map \(q(\beta)\) in \(\text{def:efficiency-handle}\).  Conversely, its simplex constraints, common-coordinate restrictions, and absorbing rows generate the observed marginal of a type-conditional Markov law on this fixed stratum; observationally null cross-potential couplings do not change any score in \(L_2(P)\).

Let \(B_P=Dq(\beta_P)\) be the full Jacobian before redundant columns are removed.  Each column sums to zero because \(\sum_{s\in\mathcal S_P}q_s(\beta)=1\).  If \(\varepsilon\mapsto\beta(\varepsilon)\) is a differentiable restricted submodel through \(\beta_P\) with velocity \(v\), differentiation gives
\[
 \dot q=B_Pv,
 \qquad
 h(s)=\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial\varepsilon}
       \log q_s\{\beta(\varepsilon)\}\right|_{\varepsilon=0}
       =\frac{(B_Pv)_s}{p_s}.                            \tag{2}
\]
Thus every restricted score belongs to \(\operatorname{col}(W_P^{-1}B_P)\).  Conversely, the relative-interior condition permits sufficiently small two-sided perturbations in every free chart direction.  Hence every column of \(W_P^{-1}B_P\), and therefore every linear combination of those columns, is a restricted score.  By construction, \(A_P\) has independent columns spanning \(\operatorname{col}(B_P)\).  Equation \((2)\) consequently proves
\[
 \mathcal T_P=\operatorname{col}(W_P^{-1}B_P)
             =\operatorname{col}(W_P^{-1}A_P)
             =\operatorname{col}(S_P).                  \tag{3}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathbf 1_{m_P}^\top W_PS_P=\mathbf 1_{m_P}^\top A_P=0\), so every vector in \((3)\) has mean zero under \(P\).  The space in \((3)\) is finite dimensional and hence closed.  Also, for every nonzero \(c\in\mathbb R^{k_P}\),
\[
 c^\top S_P^\top W_PS_Pc
 =(A_Pc)^\top W_P^{-1}(A_Pc)>0,                         \tag{4}
\]
because \(W_P^{-1}\succ0\) and \(A_P\) has full column rank.  This proves both the asserted information-matrix identity and the inverse condition used below.

By \(\text{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\), the causal target equals the observed-law functional \(\theta=\Phi(p)\) throughout the compatible fiber.  By \(\text{thm:analytic-gradient}\), for each coordinate \(\ell\) and every saturated score \(h\), and hence for every \(h\in\mathcal T_P\),
\[
 \dot\theta_{P,\ell}[h]
 =E_P\{G_{p,\ell}(O)h(O)\}
 =(G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P})^\top W_Ph.                \tag{5}
\]
The \(W_P\)-orthogonal projection of a vector \(g\in\mathbb R^{m_P}\) onto \(\operatorname{col}(S_P)\) is found by minimizing
\[
 \min_{b\in\mathbb R^{k_P}}(g-S_Pb)^\top W_P(g-S_Pb).  \tag{6}
\]
Differentiating \((6)\) gives the normal equation
\[
 S_P^\top W_PS_Pb=S_P^\top W_Pg.                        \tag{7}
\]
The coefficient matrix in \((7)\) is invertible by \((4)\).  Substituting \(g=G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}\) therefore yields
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal T_P}G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}
 =S_P(S_P^\top W_PS_P)^{-1}S_P^\top W_P
  G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P},                            \tag{8}
\]
which is the promised finite, evaluable formula.  Equations \((5)\) and \((8)\) show that
\[
 E_P\{\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}(O)h(O)\}
 =\dot\theta_{P,\ell}[h]
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\mathcal T_P.               \tag{9}
\]
If another element of \(\mathcal T_P\) represents the same derivative, its difference from \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_P\) and is orthogonal to \(\mathcal T_P\), so it is zero.  Thus \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\) is the constrained canonical gradient.

It remains to establish the lower bound and its comparison with the saturated bound.  Fix \(a\in\mathbb R^9\), and let \(\varphi_a\in L_2^0(P)\) be any scalar influence function representing the derivative of \(a^\top\theta\) along every \(h\in\mathcal T_P\).  By \((9)\),
\[
 E_P[\{\varphi_a(O)-a^\top\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)\}h(O)]=0
 \quad(h\in\mathcal T_P).                              \tag{10}
\]
Since \(a^\top\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\in\mathcal T_P\), Pythagoras and \((10)\) give
\[
 E_P\{\varphi_a(O)^2\}
 =a^\top V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)a
  +\|\varphi_a-a^\top\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\|_{L_2(P)}^2
 \ge a^\top V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)a.                      \tag{11}
\]
This proves the stated pointwise covariance lower bound without asserting that an estimator attaining it exists.

Finally set \(R_\ell=(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})G_{p,\ell}\).  Projection orthogonality gives
\[
 \Sigma_{\ell r}(p)
 =E_P\{\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}(O)
        \psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,r}(O)\}+E_P\{R_\ell(O)R_r(O)\}. \tag{12}
\]
Multiplying \((12)\) by \(a_\ell a_r\) and summing proves
\[
 a^\top\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a
 =\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^\top G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.      \tag{13}
\]
The right side of \((13)\) is positive exactly when \(a^\top G_p\notin\mathcal T_P\), proving the strictness criterion.  The construction is pointwise on a fixed relative-interior constant-rank stratum.  The class \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\) neither imposes the date-\(4\) restriction nor buffers the rank of \(A_P\) or changes of \(\mathcal S_P\); therefore no uniform constrained-efficiency conclusion follows.

added_lemmas.statement: Under cohort overlap, exactly two latent types, consistency, type-conditional first-order Markov paths, and four-slice rank, every cohort and type has positive active mass: for all \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(j\in\{1,2\}\), \(\alpha_j^d>0\).  Consequently \(\pi_j^d\geq\alpha_j^d>0\), so cohort-specific type overlap is implied rather than separately assumed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(d\in\{0,1\}\).  Cohort overlap makes conditioning on \(D=d\) well defined.  Consistency and the type-conditional first-order Markov property imply that, for every \(x,y,u,v\in\mathcal A\),
\[
 \bar A_{xy}^d[u,v]
 =\sum_{j=1}^2
 P(Z=j,X_0=u,X_1=x\mid D=d)\,
 P(X_2=y\mid X_1=x,Z=j,D=d)\,
 P(X_3=v\mid X_2=y,Z=j,D=d).                            \tag{14}
\]
For fixed \((x,y,d)\), each summand in \((14)\) is an outer product of a two-vector indexed by \(u\) and a two-vector indexed by \(v\), multiplied by the scalar middle transition probability.  Suppose \(\alpha_{j_0}^d=0\) for one type \(j_0\).  By the definition of \(\alpha_{j_0}^d\),
\[
 P(Z=j_0,X_1=x\mid D=d)=0\qquad(x\in\mathcal A),        \tag{15}
\]
so every first factor for type \(j_0\) in \((14)\) is zero.  Because there are exactly two types, \((14)\) then contains at most one nonzero outer product.  Hence \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar A_{xy}^d)\leq1\), contradicting the assumed positive smallest singular value of each \(2\times2\) matrix \(\bar A_{xy}^d\).  Thus \(\alpha_j^d>0\) for both types.  Finally,
\[
 \pi_j^d=P(Z=j\mid D=d)
 \geq P(Z=j,X_1\in\mathcal A\mid D=d)=\alpha_j^d>0.      \tag{16}
\]
Since \(d\) was arbitrary, the conclusion holds in both cohorts.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) lie in the relative interior of a fixed structural support stratum on which the observed-cell factor map in \(\text{def:efficiency-handle}\) has locally constant rank \(k_P\).  For the actual support \(\mathcal S_P\), construct \(A_P\), \(W_P\), and \(S_P=W_P^{-1}A_P\) as in that definition.  Then
\[
 \mathcal T_P=\operatorname{col}(S_P),
 \qquad S_P^\top W_PS_P=A_P^\top W_P^{-1}A_P\succ0.
\]
For \(G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}=(G_{p,\ell}(s))_{s\in\mathcal S_P}\), the constrained canonical gradient is computable coordinatewise by
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}
 =S_P(S_P^\top W_PS_P)^{-1}S_P^\top W_PG_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}.
\]
The target is \(\theta=\Phi(p)\), and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=E_P\{\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)^\top\}\) is the pointwise covariance lower bound among mean-zero influence vectors representing the derivative of \(\theta\) along \(\mathcal T_P\).  Moreover, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^9\),
\[
 a^\top\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a
 =\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^\top G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.
\]
Consequently the constrained bound is strictly smaller than the saturated bound in direction \(a\) exactly when \(a^\top G_p\notin\mathcal T_P\).  This result neither asserts existence of an attaining restricted-model estimator nor establishes uniform constrained efficiency over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim ranges over unspecified tangent-space points and asserts attainment without an explicit restricted likelihood or an estimator construction. The corrected claim restricts to the relative interior of a fixed-support, locally constant-rank stratum of the same class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\), supplies the cell-factor Jacobian and score matrix, and proves the computable canonical-gradient lower bound. It deletes only the unsupported estimator-attainment and uniformity implications; the regular stratum is a subset of the original class, not a substitute for a published class.

proposed.name: Explicit fifth-date restricted score construction
proposed.construction:
For a law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\), let \(\mathcal S_P=\{s:p_s>0\}\) be its actual observed support.  On a fixed structural support stratum, form a finite structural chart \(\beta\) as follows.  Its coordinates are one-omitted-category coordinates for the cohort probabilities \(\delta_d=P(D=d)\), the conditional type probabilities \(\pi_j^d\), the initial probabilities \(\mu_j^d(x)=P(X_0=x\mid Z=j,D=d)\), and every nondegenerate row of \(H_j^d,Q_j,U_j,V_j,L_j\) and of an unrestricted treated date-\(4\) kernel \(T_{4,j}^1\).  All coordinates forbidden by \(\mathcal G\), all absorbing rows, and all zero coordinates defining the stratum are held fixed; omitted coordinates are filled by the row-sum-one constraints.  Write \(T_{3,j}^0=U_j\), \(T_{3,j}^1=V_j\), and \(T_{4,j}^0=L_j\).  For \(s=(d,x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)\in\mathcal S_P\), define the observed-cell factor map
\[
 q_s(\beta)=\delta_d\sum_{j=1}^2\pi_j^d\mu_j^d(x_0)
 H_j^d[x_0,x_1]Q_j[x_1,x_2]
 T_{3,j}^d[x_2,x_3]T_{4,j}^d[x_3,x_4].
\]
All occurrences of \(Q_j\) share the same coordinates across cohorts.  The coordinates \(U_j\) and \(L_j\) appearing in observed control cells also parameterize the treated cohort's untreated counterfactual kernels; those counterfactual copies are observationally null but impose the full-data common-kernel restrictions.  At \(P\), differentiate this displayed polynomial map with respect to every free chart coordinate.  If its Jacobian has rank \(k_P\), retain any \(k_P\) independent columns spanning its column space and call the resulting \(|\mathcal S_P|\times k_P\) matrix \(A_P\).  Define
\[
 W_P=\operatorname{diag}\{p_s:s\in\mathcal S_P\},
 \qquad S_P=W_P^{-1}A_P.
\]
The handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{eff}}\) is this finite factor-map, Jacobian-selection, and weighted-score construction.  Observationally null coordinates of the full-data law are discarded before the independent columns are selected.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The prior handle said only to differentiate unspecified restrictions. This replacement exposes the full five-date latent-mixture product, all simplex and absorbing constraints, shared kernel coordinates, Jacobian reduction, and weighted score matrix.

proposed.name: Broad absorbing support model
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}=\{P:P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:consistency},\text{ass:no-anticipation},\text{ass:two-types},\text{ass:cohort-overlap},\text{ass:markov-paths},\text{ass:absorbing-exit},\text{ass:common-date-two-transition},\text{ass:common-first-post-untreated-transition},\text{ass:four-slice-rank},\text{ and }\text{ass:simple-cycle-spectrum}\}\).  Date-\(1\) absorption is allowed, and no date-\(4\) common-kernel restriction is imposed.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Four-slice rank with exactly two types already forces positive cohort-specific active type mass, so type overlap is a derived property rather than a class assumption.

proposed.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\), the recovery map is well-defined and \(\Phi(p)=	heta=(
u_1^	op,
u_2^	op,	au^	op)^	op\).  More strongly, throughout \(\mathcal F(p)\) the formulas recover, in the common descending cycle-product order, \(\alpha_j^d\), \(s_j^d\), every active row of \(Q_j\) and \(R_j^d\), the complete unnormalized component law of \((Z,X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3)\) on \(\{X_1\in\mathcal A\}\), every contribution \(
u_j\), every at-risk effect \(\eta_j=

u_j\).  Units with \(X_1=e\) have zero treatment effect by no anticipation and absorption.  No time-homogeneity or date-\(4\) common-kernel condition is required.  The theorem does not assert identification of \(\pi_j^d\) or of the full conditional effect \(	au_j\) when date-\(1\) absorption is possible.
proposed.justification: This is the maximal identification theorem: four-slice rank itself supplies positive active type mass, and omitted initially absorbed units have zero effect and therefore cannot disturb active type contributions or the aggregate.
proposed.gap: Adjacent spectral theorems exclude the absorbing terminal boundary and do not isolate the aggregate-versus-full-conditional frontier under latent initial absorption.
proposed.consumer: An incumbent-firm panel may report latent-type contributions and the aggregate even when the latent allocation of firms already exited at the cut is not recoverable.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the redundant type-overlap dependency by the proved consequence of four-slice rank; the claim is unchanged.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\) that also satisfies \(\texttt{ass:no-date-one-absorption}\), the recovery map is well-defined and \(\Phi(p)=\theta\). In addition, \(\alpha_j^d=\pi_j^d\), and throughout \(\mathcal F(p)\) the formulas recover the same type masses, the same full component law of \((Z,X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3)\) in each cohort, the same full conditional type effects \(\tau_j=\nu_j/\pi_j^1\), and the same aggregate \(\tau\), up to the declared descending \(\rho_j^d\) order. This corollary requires neither time homogeneity nor a date-\(4\) common untreated kernel and remains valid when the common absorbing row violates all-state terminal-rank and positive-transition conditions.
proposed.justification: This corollary shows exactly what the observable no-date-\(1\)-absorption condition buys: active masses become full type masses and at-risk effects become full conditional type effects.
proposed.gap: Existing full-rank reconstruction does not prove this upgrade on a structurally singular common-absorbing terminal factor.
proposed.consumer: Full latent-type conditional effects are justified only when the observed panel verifies absence of absorption at the recovery cut.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corollary obtains positive type masses through the active-frontier theorem and no longer needs the deleted redundant assumption directly.

proposed.statement:
The exact law \(\omega^\star\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\) and also satisfies \(\texttt{ass:no-date-one-absorption}\).  It has
\[
K^0=K^1=\begin{pmatrix}29/5&-12/5\\8/5&1/5\end{pmatrix}
\]
with ordered spectrum \((5,1)\), full conditional type effects
\[
\tau_1=(1/25,0,-1/25),\quad
\tau_2=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20),
\]
and aggregate effect \(\tau=(3/400,-1/80,1/200)\).  Its at-risk masses satisfy \(\alpha_j^d=1/2\), its type contributions are
\[
\nu_1=(1/50,0,-1/50),\quad
\nu_2=(-1/80,-1/80,1/40),
\]
and its at-risk effects satisfy \(\eta_j=\tau_j\).

The laws \(P^A\) and \(P^B\) both belong to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\), induce the same observed five-date law, satisfy \(P^A(X_1=e\mid D=d)=P^B(X_1=e\mid D=d)=1/5\), and have the same active-slice arrays and the same displayed cycle product.  Their full type shares are, in both cohorts,
\[
(\pi_1^{A,d},\pi_2^{A,d})=(3/5,2/5),\quad
(\pi_1^{B,d},\pi_2^{B,d})=(2/5,3/5),
\]
and their full conditional type effects are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_1^A&=(2/75,0,-2/75),&
\tau_2^A&=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20),\\
\tau_1^B&=(1/25,0,-1/25),&
\tau_2^B&=(-1/60,-1/60,1/30).
\end{aligned}
\]
Nevertheless the two laws have the same at-risk masses \(\alpha_1^d=\alpha_2^d=2/5\), the same type contributions
\[
\nu_1=(2/125,0,-2/125),\quad
\nu_2=(-1/100,-1/100,1/50),
\]
the same at-risk effects
\[
\eta_1=(1/25,0,-1/25),\quad
\eta_2=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20),
\]
and the same entire aggregate ATT vector \(\tau=(3/500,-1/100,1/250)\).  Together with \(\texttt{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\), this observational-equivalence pair proves the sharp frontier: the broad absorbing model identifies active masses, unnormalized type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate ATT, but it does not identify full type shares or full conditional type effects; adding \(\texttt{ass:no-date-one-absorption}\) removes exactly this allocation ambiguity.
proposed.justification: The witness establishes nonvacuity, checks every normalization exactly, and identifies the precise role of the initial support face for the conditional targets.
proposed.gap: Existing absorbing-outcome difference-in-differences results do not provide a two-type multi-state observational-equivalence calculation, and generic mixture results do not isolate the initial-absorber allocation that breaks conditional ATT recovery.
proposed.consumer: Applied researchers can treat baseline exit as a falsifiable support diagnostic and avoid interpreting conditional latent-type effects when baseline absorbers are present.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The explicit witness verifies its positive masses directly and does not consume a separate model-wide type-overlap assumption.

The new lemma proves cohort-specific type overlap from exactly two types, cohort overlap, Markov factorization, and nonsingular active slices, so retaining it as an independent assumption is redundant.

proposed.comparator_claim: Proposition 14 reconstructs latent transition components under its stated full-rank and positive-transition identification conditions.
proposed.matched_by: The active-frontier recovery theorem extends the inverse-cancellation architecture to the excluded common-absorbing boundary and proves the aggregate-versus-full-conditional frontier.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 reconstructs Markov-mixture components under time-homogeneous and full component-rank conditions.
proposed.matched_by: The active-frontier theorem uses active minors and stochastic normalization without time homogeneity and does not claim to subsume the published mixture theorem.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper studies homogeneous Markov-mixture reconstruction under its state-count and nondegeneracy restrictions.
proposed.matched_by: The present result is a causal, time-varying absorbing-boundary theorem for two active states and one exit state, outside that restricted reconstruction regime.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper develops aggregate duration difference-in-differences under absorption-oriented restrictions.
proposed.matched_by: The present theorem instead reconstructs latent-type multi-state contributions and isolates which conditional type effects fail with initial absorbers.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper estimates latent conditional moments by simultaneous diagonalization and derives regular asymptotics for estimated weights.
proposed.matched_by: The analytic-gradient theorem differentiates the absorbing-boundary row-sum and pseudoinverse contribution map on its enlarged support stratum.

prose_updates.tldr:
Four matched active-state slices identify the unnormalized latent-type sublaws among units active at date \(1\), even when a common absorbing state makes all-state terminal factors singular and some units are already absorbed. Spectral projectors fix scale, terminal row sums recover exit probabilities, and a full-row-rank pseudoinverse transports the second active predecessor factor. Four-slice rank itself forces positive active mass for both types in both cohorts, so separate type overlap is unnecessary. Absorption plus no anticipation makes initially absorbed units' treatment effects zero, and the type contributions \(
u_j\), at-risk effects \(
u_j/\alpha_j^1\), and aggregate ATT \(	au=\sum_j
u_j\) are point identified over the broad fiber. The observable no-date-\(1\)-absorption subface additionally identifies full type masses and conditional type effects. The analytic \(126\)-cell map has a saturated multinomial canonical gradient and guarded multiplier bands; on regular fixed-support strata of the separate fifth-date subclass, an explicit latent-mixture Jacobian gives a computable constrained influence-function lower bound, without an estimator-attainment claim.

project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit projector, row-sum, and pseudoinverse map for active component sublaws, type contributions, at-risk type effects, and the aggregate ATT on the broad absorbing class; proves that slice rank supplies active type overlap; gives a no-initial-absorption corollary for full conditional type effects and an exact sharp-frontier witness; derives an analytic saturated gradient and uniform guarded multiplier bands; and supplies an explicit product-Jacobian formula for the pointwise constrained influence bound on regular fifth-date strata.

sampling_model.overlap: Both cohorts have positive probability. Exactly two types and nonsingularity of the active slices imply positive active mass \(\alpha_j^d\), and therefore positive full mass \(\pi_j^d\), for each type and cohort; type overlap is not separately assumed.

prose_updates.related_work: Ahn and Kasahara (2026), Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, provide the closest causal setup and inverse-cancellation architecture, but their stated full-rank and positive-transition hypothesis class excludes the common absorbing boundary; the present result is an excluded-boundary extension, not an application of that class. Higgins and Jochmans (2023) and Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016) reconstruct Markov mixtures under their respective time-homogeneity, component-rank, state-count, and nondegeneracy regimes; those scaling and label ideas are prior art, while the present theorem is a causal, time-varying active-minor result and does not subsume them. Restricted hidden-Markov measurement results likewise answer reconstruction questions under their own emission or structural restrictions, not the potential-path contribution identity proved here. Deaner and Ku (2026) motivate transition restrictions for absorbing duration outcomes but study aggregate duration difference-in-differences rather than latent-type multi-state reconstruction. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017) motivate differentiating diagonalization estimators; Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, 2015) provide neighboring Gaussian bootstrap and anti-concentration tools. Newey (1990) provides the general tangent-space efficiency framework; here the restricted observed-cell product map, its independent Jacobian columns, and the weighted projection are written explicitly on regular fixed-support strata, while attainment is not claimed. Rao and Risch (2026) are the interpretation consumer: an incumbent-firm panel could use active productivity states and exit to study offsetting latent-type contributions, but this note does not claim their data satisfy its model or independent sampling assumptions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance \(\Sigma(p)\) is the efficiency bound for the specified off-model continuation \(\Phi\) in the saturated multinomial support-stratum model. On a regular fixed-support, locally constant-rank stratum of the fifth-date constrained Markov model, the explicit cell-factor Jacobian gives the pointwise canonical-gradient covariance lower bound. No attaining restricted-model estimator is constructed. The broad buffered class neither imposes the date-\(4\) restriction nor controls restricted Jacobian rank or support changes, so the calculation is not a uniform constrained-efficiency result. The exact multiplier quantile is the mathematical object; a fixed number of Monte Carlo draws needs a separate approximation-error analysis. The sharp-frontier pair changes full latent type shares and full conditional type effects while preserving active shares, at-risk effects, both contribution vectors, and the entire aggregate ATT vector.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proposal proves a sufficient constructive frontier for two known latent types, two active states, one absorbing exit, four nonsingular matched active slices, simple common cycle signatures, cohort overlap, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths, no anticipation, and common untreated date-\(2\) and first-post kernels. Four-slice rank implies positive active and full type masses, so type overlap is derived rather than imposed. The result does not establish necessity beyond the explicit initial-absorption pair, identify unknown type count, handle weak eigengaps, justify clustered policy-panel inference, or allow approximate common transitions. Full conditional type effects require the observable no-date-\(1\)-absorption subface; the broad class identifies active sublaws, type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate. Date-\(4\) common-kernel information appears only in the separately named constrained subclass, where the paper gives a pointwise regular-stratum influence-bound computation but no attaining estimator or uniform efficiency theorem.

statement_notes.justification: The explicit latent-mixture product Jacobian turns the pointwise restricted tangent calculation into an evaluable weighted projection on regular fixed-support strata.
statement_notes.gap: The broad class neither imposes the date-\(4\) common kernel nor buffers restricted Jacobian rank or support changes, and no attaining restricted estimator is constructed.
statement_notes.consumer: A specified fifth-date likelihood can compute the pointwise influence-function lower bound from its cell Jacobian; the broad guarded bands remain the proved inferential procedure.
